title: Lovin' Cup
venue_description:
Lovin' Cup

Lovin' Cup is a bistro and brewery at Park Point near the Rochester Institute of Technology, combining a full kitchen and house-brewed beer with a genuinely professional concert setup — a proper stage, sound system and stage lighting rarely found at a restaurant this size.

Atmosphere and Setting

The venue markets itself around an “all-encompassing, sensory experience,” and the room backs that up: comfortable bistro seating that turns into a genuine concert audience once the stage lights come up, with a menu and drink list that keeps people around well past their own performance slot.

Open Mic Night

Lovin' Cup has hosted a free, weekly open mic every Tuesday night since 2009, making it one of the longest-running recurring music nights in Rochester. Sign-up begins at 6:30 PM ahead of a 7:00 PM start, and the night welcomes singers, songwriters, instrumentalists, comedians, poets, storytellers and dancers alike. The format is intentionally low-tech — no full bands, drum kits or large amplifiers — which keeps turnover quick and gives more performers a turn. A house piano is available, and microphones are sanitized between each act.

Other Programming

Outside of the Tuesday open mic, Lovin' Cup books a steady stream of touring and regional bands, taking full advantage of its professional-grade stage and sound system.

For Performers

Because sign-ups run first-come, first-served and the show has a loyal following of regulars, arriving close to 6:30 PM is the best way to guarantee a spot.

Good to Know

Lovin' Cup is located at 300 Park Point Drive, Rochester, NY 14623. The venue is closed Sundays; the open mic runs every Tuesday.

title: Bernunzio Uptown Music
venue_description:
Bernunzio Uptown Music

Bernunzio Uptown Music is a vintage and used instrument specialist on East Avenue with roughly 50 years of history buying, selling and repairing guitars, banjos, mandolins and ukuleles from makers like Martin, Gibson, Fender and Epiphone. It's a destination shop for serious players, but it's also become a genuine community hub for acoustic music in Rochester.

Atmosphere and Setting

The shop's back room, normally used for lessons and instrument demos, transforms into an informal jam space on jam days — walls lined with vintage instruments rather than a typical bar or brewery backdrop, which gives the sessions a distinctly musician-focused feel.

Bluegrass Jam

On second Saturdays from noon to 3:00 PM, Bernunzio hosts an Intermediate+ Bluegrass Jam. The first hour runs at a slower tempo with guided repertoire aimed at intermediate players, while the remaining two hours pick up the pace for intermediate-to-advanced pickers, with an emphasis on soloing, trading breaks and ear training around a core set of traditional bluegrass standards.

Other Programming

Beyond the monthly bluegrass jam, the shop hosts additional acoustic sessions and clinics tied to its vintage-instrument inventory, and its buy-sell-trade counter draws musicians from well beyond Rochester.

For Performers

The jam is a drop-in format with no formal sign-up, but it does assume a baseline of playing ability given the “intermediate-plus” framing — beginners are welcome to observe and learn.

Good to Know

Bernunzio Uptown Music is located at 122 East Ave, Rochester, NY 14604. Free street parking is available, along with additional parking in the East End Garage directly behind the store.

title: Vine & Tap Wine Bar
venue_description:
Vine & Tap Wine Bar

Vine & Tap is a wine bar in Rochester's lakeside Charlotte neighborhood, built around a rotating menu of wine, beer and charcuterie sourced from across the Finger Lakes region. Guided tastings and curated flights round out a spot that leans into a relaxed, food-and-drink-forward atmosphere.

Atmosphere and Setting

The room favors conversation and unhurried evenings over a typical bar-and-stage setup, which suits its Friday night jazz programming well — more listening room than concert hall, with wine and small plates close at hand.

Jazz On Tap

Every Friday from 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM, Vine & Tap hosts Jazz On Tap, featuring a rotating lineup of local jazz musicians. The relaxed format makes it approachable both for listeners settling in for the evening and for musicians looking for a low-key room to play or sit in.

Other Programming

Vine & Tap also books local bands on Saturday nights, giving the wine bar a full weekend of live music alongside its wine and charcuterie program.

For Performers

Because the lineup rotates, check the venue's website or social media ahead of time for the specific week's musicians.

Good to Know

Vine & Tap Wine Bar is located at 4768 Lake Ave, Rochester, NY 14612, in the Charlotte neighborhood near the Lake Ontario waterfront. It's closed on Wednesdays.

title: Main Place Tavern
venue_description:
Main Place Tavern

Main Place Tavern is a neighborhood bar on East Main Street on Rochester's east side, offering a casual, unpretentious setting with a full bar menu and a loyal local following.

Atmosphere and Setting

The tavern has the feel of a classic corner bar — friendly, low-key and community-oriented, which makes it a natural home for a recurring blues jam built around regulars and musicians who know each other well.

Open Blues Jam

Every Sunday evening from 6:30 PM to 9:30 PM, the nonprofit Blues Society of Western New York hosts an Open Blues Jam at Main Place Tavern. Musicians of all skill levels are invited to sit in with a house band and work through blues standards in front of an appreciative crowd, making it one of the most reliable blues jams in the Rochester area.

Other Programming

Main Place Tavern also hosts occasional live band nights tied to Rochester's broader blues and bar-band scene.

For Performers

Because the jam is organized by the Blues Society of Western New York, it draws a mix of society members and newcomers, and it's a good entry point for musicians looking to connect with the region's blues community.

Good to Know

Main Place Tavern is located at 1899 E Main St, Rochester, NY 14609. Check the Blues Society of Western New York's website to confirm the jam is running before visiting, since it is organized by a third-party nonprofit rather than the bar itself.
